title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — General Assessment #17

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #17
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Properties of Matter? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Properties of Matter.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Properties of Matter.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Properties of Matter.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Properties of Matter.

2. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Removing all vegetation
   C. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   D. Overgrazing continuously

3. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Milk souring
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Ice melting to water
   D. Iron rusting

4. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

5. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

6. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Decomposers only
   B. Tertiary consumers
   C. Primary consumers only
   D. Producers

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Heat? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Heat.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Heat.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Heat.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Heat.

8. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. pascal (Pa)
   B. newton (N)
   C. watt (W)
   D. joule (J)

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Light? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Light.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Light.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Light.

10. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Movement of water only across a membrane
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. A chemical reaction forming ash

11. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Only water vapour

12. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 37 °C
   C. 0 °C
   D. 50 °C

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Heat and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Properties of Matter and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Water Conservation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Properties of Matter.

2. C — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

3. C — Ice melting to water

4. B — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

5. B — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

6. D — Producers

7. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Heat.

8. B — newton (N)

9. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.

10. B — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

11. B — Glucose and oxygen

12. A — 100 °C

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Heat; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Properties of Matter; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Water Conservation; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Light; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
